claim: A door that opens by lifting its ceiling almost always has a roofed ceiling: its ceiling IS the moving part, and as sky it would be a hole in the roof showing daylight in a building. A door that opens by dropping its floor may be open to the sky (a gate in an outdoor wall). Of the campaign's Z-motion sectors (600/602) 6 of 779 that move their ceiling are open to the sky (0.8%, all six in E6M4), against 95 of 658 that move their floor (14.4%).
evidence: knowledge/blood/findings/probes/audit2_ceiling_movers_sky.py (run from the root with PYTHONPATH=.): over the 43 campaign maps, every type 600/602 sector with an XSECTOR, moving ceiling = off_ceiling_z != on_ceiling_z, open = ceiling_stat bit 0: 6/779 (all E6M4) against 95/658
bloodmap/rules_blood.py:614-653, rule 'ceiling-mover-is-not-open-to-the-sky', states the same counts
both poses rendered when the rule was written (its first version asserted the opposite)
use: Give a ceiling-lifting door a real ceiling; use a floor-dropping gate under the sky.

checked.how: Ran knowledge/blood/findings/probes/audit2_ceiling_movers_sky.py over the 43 campaign maps (types 600/602 with an XSECTOR, ceiling moves = on_ceiling_z != off_ceiling_z, sky = ceiling_stat bit 0): ceiling movers 6/779 open to the sky (0.8%), all 6 in E6M4; floor movers 95/658 (14.4%). Read bloodmap/rules_blood.py:614-653 (_ceiling_movers_are_not_open_to_the_sky, rule text): it now gives the same 95/658 and 6/779.
